items.title: Finite-budget nonlinear FAS two-grid cycle
items.statement:
Let $U_h\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_h}$ and $U_H\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_H}$ be open,
with $n_h,n_H\ge1$. Let $F_h:U_h\to\mathbb R^{n_h}$ and
$F_H:U_H\to\mathbb R^{n_H}$ be residual maps, and let $f_h\in\mathbb R^{n_h}$.
The equation on the fine level is $F_h(u)=f_h$. Choose linear maps
$I: \mathbb R^{n_h}\to\mathbb R^{n_H}$ (iterate restriction),
$R: \mathbb R^{n_h}\to\mathbb R^{n_H}$ (residual restriction), and
$P: \mathbb R^{n_H}\to\mathbb R^{n_h}$ (prolongation). No equality among
$I$, $R$, and $P$ is imposed by this definition. Choose positive diagonal
matrices $D^{\rm pre}$ and $D^{\rm post}$, damping factors
$0<\omega_{\rm pre},\omega_{\rm post}\le1$, finite sweep counts
$\nu_{\rm pre},\nu_{\rm post}\in\mathbb N_0$, a finite positive coarse-solver
operation budget $B_H$, and a positive integer $\gamma$.

A **coarse-solver call** with target $g\in\mathbb R^{n_H}$ and initial value
$z\in U_H$ must return within $B_H$ declared operations either an exact selected
root $(v,\texttt{exact-root},0)$ with $F_H(v)=g$, an inexact value
$(v,\texttt{inexact-root},\eta)$ with the explicitly computed residual
$\eta=\|F_H(v)-g\|_2>0$, or one of
$\texttt{branch-failure}$, $\texttt{domain-failure}$, and
$\texttt{budget-exhausted}$. The solver contract requires it to return the
initial value unchanged as `exact-root` when $F_H(z)=g$ and $z$ is the selected
root. A direct formula, an exact local branch, or a finite iterative solver may
be supplied; the definition makes no claim that any solver finds a root from an
arbitrary initial value.

For a starting fine iterate $u\in U_h$, do the following in exact real
arithmetic.

1. Perform $\nu_{\rm pre}$ nonlinear damped-Jacobi sweeps. In each sweep,
form the trial value
$$\widetilde u:=u-\omega_{\rm pre}(D^{\rm pre})^{-1}(F_h(u)-f_h).$$
If $\widetilde u\notin U_h$, return the current valid fine iterate $u$ with
status `domain-failure`; otherwise set $u:=\widetilde u$.

2. Set $u_H=Iu$. If $u_H\notin U_H$, return the last valid fine iterate
with status `domain-failure`. Otherwise set $r_h=f_h-F_h(u)$ and
$$g_H=F_H(u_H)+Rr_h=Rf_h+\tau(u),\qquad \tau(u):=F_H(Iu)-RF_h(u).$$

3. Set $z=u_H$ and initialize a finite diagnostic list $\Delta=()$. For
$t=1,\ldots,\gamma$, call the declared coarse solver on $(g_H,z,B_H)$. On
`branch-failure`, `domain-failure`, or `budget-exhausted`, return the last
valid fine iterate with that status and the diagnostics accumulated so far.
On `exact-root` or `inexact-root`, append the returned status and residual to
$\Delta$, replace $z$ by the returned value, and append any nested diagnostics
returned by the coarse call. Reusing $g_H$ while starting at the current $z$
makes repeated coarse calls a bounded V/W-style cycle.

4. Form the trial correction
$$\widetilde u:=u+P(z-Iu).$$
If $\widetilde u\notin U_h$, return the current valid fine iterate $u$ with
status `domain-failure` and $\Delta$; otherwise set $u:=\widetilde u$.

5. Perform $\nu_{\rm post}$ nonlinear damped-Jacobi sweeps. In each sweep,
form the trial value
$$\widetilde u:=u-\omega_{\rm post}(D^{\rm post})^{-1}(F_h(u)-f_h).$$
If $\widetilde u\notin U_h$, return the current valid fine iterate $u$ with
status `domain-failure` and $\Delta$; otherwise set $u:=\widetilde u$.
Compute the final fine residual
$\eta_h:=\|F_h(u)-f_h\|_2$. Return the resulting iterate with status
`exact-root` and residual $0$ if $\eta_h=0$, and with status `inexact-root`
and residual $\eta_h$ if $\eta_h>0$, together with $\Delta$. Thus the status
used when this procedure is called recursively
always certifies the residual for its own level equation; zero residuals
reported by inner coarse calls do not by themselves certify that the returned
fine iterate is a root.

Every loop count and solver budget is finite. `V` and `W` refer to the cases
$\gamma=1$ and $\gamma=2$. A multi-level cycle uses this two-grid procedure at
each level, with the next-level cycle supplied as the coarse solver and a
finite level cap. Fixed-point consistency, linear reduction, local convergence,
and work bounds are separate claims.

items.title: Second derivative formula for a composed cycle map
items.statement: For C2 maps S, C, and T between compatible finite-dimensional Euclidean open sets, the second derivative of E=T∘C∘S is the sum of the outer second-derivative term and the derivative of the inner composition’s second derivative.
items.strategy: Differentiate the first-derivative composition identity using the bounded bilinear product rule, then apply the result twice.

references.title: Chin-Lung Wang, Banach Calculus, §§2.1.1–2.1.4 and §2.3

items.title: Finite-budget recursive nonlinear FAS V/W cycle
items.statement: On a finite hierarchy, use the two-grid FAS update at every noncoarsest level, recurse on the next level with the current full coarse approximation, and use a finite-budget base solver whose exact/inexact statuses report the base residual and preserve an initial exact root. A recursive cycle reports its own level residual through the coarse-solver interface and retains nested coarse residual diagnostics. The V-cycle has one recursive call and the W-cycle two.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes
Van Emden Henson, Multigrid Methods for Nonlinear Problems: An Overview, UCRL-JC-150259

items.title: Derivative of the exact-branch FAS two-grid cycle
items.statement: For a C1 fine/coarse residual pair and linear transfers, if the selected coarse root at a fine root has invertible coarse Jacobian and the pre/post smoothers are C1, the implicit coarse branch is C1 and the derivative of the actual exact-branch two-grid cycle is the composition of the two smoother derivatives with I - P DF_H(Iu*)^{-1} R DF_h(u*).
items.strategy: Differentiate the coarse equation by the Euclidean implicit function theorem, then apply the chain rule to the correction and both smoothers.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6

items.title: A finite FAS V/W cycle terminates with bounded stated work
items.statement: For a finite hierarchy with finite pre/post sweep counts, finite recursive cycle count, finite base-solver budget, and terminating residual/transfer/update primitives, the recursive FAS V/W procedure returns a residual-certified status after finitely many calls. Its work is bounded by the explicit level recurrence, which includes nonlinear smoothing, coarse solves, and returned diagnostic bookkeeping.
items.strategy: Induct on the level and count each bounded smoother, recursive call, transfer, correction, and base-solver operation.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6

items.title: An exact fine root is fixed by the FAS V/W cycle
items.statement: If every chosen nonlinear smoother fixes an exact root, each restriction lies in the next-level domain and is selected as the zero-defect coarse root, and the base solver preserves any initial exact root, then the exact-branch FAS V/W cycle leaves every fine root fixed. No algebraic relation among I, R, and P is needed.
items.strategy: Induct over the hierarchy and substitute the exact fine root into each tau-corrected coarse equation.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes
Van Emden Henson, Multigrid Methods for Nonlinear Problems: An Overview, UCRL-JC-150259

items.title: A smooth FAS cycle converges locally under its actual derivative bounds
items.statement: Let E be the actual exact-branch error map of a fixed FAS cycle with root u*, ||DE(u*)||=q<1, and ||DE(x)-DE(y)||<=L||x-y|| on a convex radius-r ball. If q+Lr/2<1, then E maps that ball into itself and every iterate contracts its distance to u* by the factor q+Lr/2. Mesh-independent constants must be verified uniformly in the mesh parameter.
items.strategy: Apply the mean-value integral formula to E and bound the derivative variation by L times the distance from the root.

items.title: A linear Galerkin V/W cycle is translation-covariant
items.statement: For a finite SPD Galerkin hierarchy and residual-correction pre/post updates, shifting the initial iterate by a and the right side by A_j a shifts the returned finite V/W-cycle iterate by exactly a.
items.strategy: Compare the two runs level by level, using invariant residuals and identical deterministic coarse-error inputs.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes

items.title: Linear FAS exactly reduces to a Galerkin correction V/W cycle
items.statement: On a finite SPD Galerkin hierarchy with R_j=P_j^T and A_{j-1}=P_j^T A_j P_j, linear residual-correction pre/post smoothers, and exact coarse solves, the recursive FAS V/W-cycle produces exactly the iterate returned by the corresponding linear Galerkin correction V/W-cycle with the same sweep counts and cycle count.
items.strategy: Induct on levels, subtract A_H Iu from the tau-corrected coarse equation, and identify the resulting coarse residual-correction equation.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes

items.title: An inexact FAS coarse solve contributes a bounded correction defect
items.statement: If the selected exact coarse root v(u) satisfies a residual-to-solution bound ||vhat-v(u)||<=M_H eta, where eta=||F_H(vhat)-g_H(u)||, then the prolongated correction differs from the exact-branch correction by at most ||P|| M_H eta. Under an exact-cycle contraction factor kappa, successive inexact cycles satisfy ||e_{k+1}||<=kappa||e_k||+||P||M_H eta_k.
items.strategy: Subtract the exact and inexact coarse corrections and apply the declared residual-to-solution bound and prolongation norm.

items.title: A two-node semilinear diffusion FAS cycle has an explicit local rate
items.statement: For the h=1 two-node finite-difference discretization of -u''+u^3=0 on (0,3) with zero endpoint values, the exact-branch Galerkin FAS two-grid map with P=(1,1)^T, I=(1/2,1/2), R=P^T, and one pre/post weighted nonlinear-Jacobi sweep fixes the unique root and is a contraction on the radius-1/100 Euclidean ball, with factor at most 27/400.
items.strategy: Compute the strong monotonicity, exact coarse branch, cycle derivative, and a uniform second-derivative bound on the stated ball.

references.title: William L. Briggs, Van Emden Henson, and Steve F. McCormick, A Multigrid Tutorial, 2nd ed., Chapter 6
Harald van Brummelen, Basics of Multigrid Methods, SINTEF winter-school lecture notes

items.title: The tau term recovers the restricted root in reaction Poisson
items.statement: For F(u)=Au+u^{\circ 3}, A=[[2,-1],[-1,2]], P=(1,1)^T, I=(1/2,1/2), R=P^T, and the manufactured fine root u*=(1,0), the tau-corrected FAS coarse equation selects Iu*=1/2 exactly; its tau value is -3/4.
items.strategy: Substitute the manufactured fine root into the fine residual, restricted residual, coarse operator, and tau expression.

items.title: Omitting tau can move an exact fine root
items.statement: The assertion that replacing the tau-corrected coarse right side by the restricted fine right side always preserves an exact fine-grid root is false.
items.strategy: Use an SPD two-node fine matrix and a rediscretized coarse scalar operator that differs from its Galerkin value, then compute the no-tau coarse correction exactly.

items.title: The certified FAS contraction radius shrinks at a pitchfork
items.statement: For F_mu(x,y)=(mu x+x^3,y), a coarse solve of the y component and two weighted nonlinear-Jacobi sweeps give an exact FAS cycle whose derivative norm at the root is (1-mu/2)^2 for 0<mu<=1. The local contraction theorem certifies radius r_mu=sqrt(mu/100), which tends to zero at the pitchfork mu=0.
items.strategy: Compute the coarse correction and the scalar smoother composition, then evaluate its derivative at the root.

items.title: A one-level linear FAS correction is the Galerkin correction
items.statement: For A=[[2,-1],[-1,2]], P=(1,1)^T, I=(1/2,1/2), R=P^T, and A_H=P^TAP=2, the FAS coarse difference is exactly A_H^{-1}R(f-Au), so prolongation gives the standard Galerkin coarse correction.
items.strategy: Compute the coarse residual difference and compare it with the linear correction formula.
